claims.quote: In that context, modeling RVQ tokens with an RQ-Transformer significantly improves perplexity over using separate classification heads.
claims.reason: Authors explicitly propose a new hierarchical streaming audio LM (Helium plus a smaller Transformer / RQ-Transformer). Table 5 holds delay fixed and toggles only the RQ-Transformer versus separate heads, with all models initialized from Helium and pretrained on audio, so the ablation is controlled (YES), not partial.

Page 2 states they introduce the first multi-stream audio LM that jointly models input and output streams; this is a distinct ARCH novelty from the hierarchical tokenizer model. No matched with-vs-without multi-stream comparison is reported (single-stream vs multi-stream rows in Table 7 confound pretraining with instruction tuning).

claims.quote: Both Mimi codecs are trained with distillation, and either with the same combination of reconstruction and adversarial losses as Encodec (see Section 3.3) or adversarial losses only.
claims.reason: The contribution list says they introduce improved training tricks for the codec (TRAIN objective). Table 4 compares two Mimi models that both use distillation and differ in the loss mix, with MUSHRA 81.0 vs 58.8, so this is a matched ablation (YES).

Same contribution bullet as A_only0 (new hierarchical streaming Moshi architecture). Not a separate claim; the RQ-Transformer ablation is already coded YES on A_only0. PARTIAL is too low: within each delay the only change is RQ-Transformer vs independent heads.
Same multi-stream / full-duplex contribution already kept as A_only1 (page 2 'first multi-stream' and page 3 'model several audio streams in parallel'). Not a second ARCH claim; ablation remains NO.
